Hi Alice — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap + ask for a couple of clarifications so we can put together a focused pricing proposal and mutual action plan.

Recap from today's call:
- Use case: customer-facing AI features for fraud detection & intelligent routing (high sensitivity to latency).
- Deployment preference: Private/VPC behind FintechCo VPC; likely on GCP us-central for initial rollout.
- Key non-negotiables: data isolation, KMS integration, audit logs, SLA for latency.

Open items we need to finalize pricing options (please reply inline or in a quick note):
1) Token volumes: can you confirm expected monthly token consumption — baseline and peak? (we discussed 30-50M baseline, 150-200M peak, confirm if that's right)
2) Budget range: do you have an initial target spend or target $/1M tokens you're aiming for? This helps us size the licensing vs metered tradeoffs.
3) Environments: how many separate environments will you need (prod, staging, dev, sandbox/partners)?
4) Support/SLA tier: are you targeting Standard support or do you need Premium (24x7, SLA-backed)?

What we'll propose once we get these answers:
- 2 pricing paths: (A) annual license + per-vCPU/instance fee optimized for consistent throughput, and (B) hybrid: lower license + metered tokens for bursty patterns.
- Environment-based pricing add-ons (discounts for multiple envs in same org).
- Support tier pricing and optional professional services for onboarding and SOC2 evidence collection.

Attachments: Redwood_Private_Pricing_Sheet_v3.pdf (pricing examples and licensing breakdown)

Next steps: if you can reply with the 4 items above by EOD tomorrow we'll send a tailored proposal and a 30/60/90 mutual action plan. If easier, I'm available for a 30-min follow-up Wed or Thu.

Hi Alice — thanks for the details and for looping procurement. Per your asks below I've summarized two concrete pricing paths and the unit economics examples. This is a ballpark framework; we'll convert to a formal quote once procurement confirms terms.

Quoted assumptions (to keep apples-to-apples):
- Baseline 50M tokens/mo; growth to 120M; peak bursts to 200M.
- 3 environments (prod/staging/dev); sandbox if requested adds one environment.
- Private/VPC deployment with customer-managed cloud (GCP us-central).
- Premium support required (SLA-backed).

Option A — Annual license (best for predictable, high baseline)
- Upfront annual platform license: $180,000/year (covers runtime, compile/kernels, orchestration).
- Environment add-on: $10,000/year per extra environment after first two (prod + staging included).
- Included token allocation: 1B tokens/year. Overage: $650 per 1M tokens over included allocation.
- Premium support: $45,000/year (SLA, 24x7 escalation, quarterly business reviews).

Unit economics example (year 1, baseline 50M/mo => 600M tokens/year):
- License + Premium support = $225,000/year.
- Token consumption covered by included allocation (600M < 1B) => effective $/1M tokens = $225,000 / 600 = $375 per 1M tokens.

Option B — Hybrid (lower license + metered tokens; good for bursty growth)
- Annual license: $90,000/year.
- Included token allocation: 300M tokens/year.
- Metered rate: $850 per 1M tokens over included allocation.
- Environment add-on: $8,000/year per extra environment after first two.
- Premium support: $45,000/year.

Unit economics example (year 1, 600M tokens/year):
- License + support = $135,000/year.
- Overages = 300M extra tokens -> billed at $850 per 1M = $255,000.
- Total = $390,000 => effective $/1M tokens = $390k / 600 = $650 per 1M tokens.

Notes & tradeoffs:
- If you expect to exceed ~800-900M tokens/year, Option A generally has better unit economics.
- Option B lowers up-front commitment but is higher per-token on overages — useful if you want to start smaller.
- We can add a committed token discount ladder (e.g., commit to 1B+ tokens/yr and get overage at $500 per 1M).
- Environment pricing is negotiable in multi-year agreements — we typically provide a bundled discount for 3+ environments.

Procurement asks we'll need to finalize a quote:
- Master service agreement/terms (we can send a redlineable draft).
- Purchase order process & billing contact.
- Any required SOC2/ISO evidence requests (we'll provide audit artifacts and a SOC2 report).
